html:
Tobolsk is a town in western Siberia where the Tobol River meets the Irtysh, founded by Cossacks in 1587. It stands near Isker, the capital of the Khanate of Sibir, which Yermak and his Cossacks had taken a few years before. For about two centuries it was the capital of Russian Siberia.

From Tobolsk, governors ran the fur trade and the push east that took Russia to the Pacific within sixty years (the Russian conquest of Siberia). It was the seat of Siberia's archbishop, and its white stone kremlin, built around 1700 under the mapmaker Semyon Remezov, still stands above the river. It was also a place of exile. The writer Dostoevsky passed through on his way to prison camp, and the last tsar, Nicholas II, was held here with his family in 1917 and 1918 before they were moved to Yekaterinburg and shot.

Its importance faded when the Trans-Siberian Railway passed far to the south in the 1890s, and new railway towns like Novosibirsk took the lead.
